summary.text: 新 means ‘new’ or ‘fresh’. Early forms are analyzed as 斤 (an axe) with 辛 as a sound element; some also include 木. A competing analysis treats the graph as an expansion of 𣓀, interpreted as splitting wood, so its construction remains disputed.

formation.text: One proposed analysis is phonosemantic: 斤 depicts an axe in a wood-cutting scene, while 辛 is identified as a sound component; some forms also include 木, interpreted as wood. Another proposal sees 新 as an expansion of 𣓀, interpreted as splitting wood with a wedge. The received Shuowen account and Duan Yucai’s revision parse the graph differently, so the construction remains disputed.

components.text: In one early-form analysis, 斤 represents an axe used in the proposed wood-cutting scene. The whole-graph 𣓀 analysis is a competing account, not a further component here.
Early-form analyses identify 辛 as a sound component. Its readings can be compared with 新, but these comparisons do not by themselves establish the ancient graphic analysis.

sound_limitation.text: The paleographic analysis identifies 辛 as phonetic, but the available reading comparisons do not independently establish the ancient sound relationship or settle the graph analysis.

sound.text: 辛 and 新 share the Modern Mandarin reading xīn; this modern match does not establish their ancient sound relationship.
The supplied Baxter–Sagart comparison gives both 辛 and 新 the Middle Chinese transcription sin.
The supplied Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese rows give 辛 *[s]i[n] and 新 *s.tsʰi[n]. This is a real comparison, but does not alone establish the graphic analysis.

components.text: Some early forms include 木, interpreted as wood in the proposed wood-cutting analysis. Its strokes may share a boundary with 辛, so the two are not always graphically distinct.

history.text: Early forms vary: some include 木 beside 辛, with strokes that may merge, while Warring States forms separate the elements differently. The selected seal-script and Western Zhou bronze-script images are modern redrawings of script styles, useful for comparing proposed analyses but not evidence of a settled sequence.

The received Shuowen entry glosses 新 as ‘taking wood’ and parses it with 斤 plus a phonetic element. Duan Yucai instead reads the graph as 斤 and 木 with 辛 as phonetic; paleographic analyses offer other component accounts. These historical interpretations do not settle the graph’s origin.

uncertainties.text: Proposed analyses include 斤 plus 辛, sometimes with 木; an expansion of 𣓀; and differing Shuowen and Duan Yucai parses.

One account proposes that a firewood-related word and the different word ‘new’ sounded alike or similarly, so 新 could be reused to write ‘new’. This proposed sound match remains tentative because the depicted implement’s name and pronunciation are unverified. Early inscriptions already use 新 for ‘new’; these examples neither date nor disprove the proposed borrowing.

senses.text: An oracle-bone example, 新鬯, is glossed ‘newly brewed wine’, attesting ‘new’ in the Shang corpus. This early use does not establish the character’s original meaning.
‘Recent’ and ‘modern’ are current glosses; the available account does not date their development from ‘new’.
A historical gloss and graph analysis connect 新 with taking or chopping wood for fuel, but a dated standalone use of 新 meaning ‘firewood’ is not established.

developments.text: One account proposes that a firewood-related word and the different word ‘new’ sounded alike or similarly, so the graph was reused to write ‘new’. The implement’s name and sound are unverified, and early inscriptions already use 新 for ‘new’; the proposed borrowing and its chronology therefore remain uncertain.

limitations.text: The development of ‘recent’ and ‘modern’ from ‘new’ is not dated in the available evidence.
The proposed firewood sense rests on graph analysis and a historical gloss; no dated standalone use or original pronunciation for the depicted implement is established.

items.period: Shuowen seal-script style; stylized historical form, not a dated artifact image
items.caption: This seal-script-style redraw presents the received dictionary form of 新. It provides a visual comparison for the competing accounts of the graph, but does not resolve whether its structure reflects 斤 with 辛, sometimes accompanied by 木, or an expansion of 𣓀.
items.alt: Black seal-script-style 新, with a short top stroke, a dense middle structure and a long curved stroke descending at the right.
items.selection_reason: It makes the received dictionary form available for comparison with the competing analyses of 新; its modern redraw cannot establish which analysis is correct.
items.rights: Public domain release for the SVG representation; Commons description cites a Richard Sears source image.

items.caption: This Western Zhou bronze-script-style redraw shows a form of 新 amid reported variation in early forms. It is relevant to discussions of the graph’s components, but does not establish a single sequence or settle the competing origin analyses.
items.alt: Black bronze-script-style 新, with a short top stroke, a broad complex structure on the left and a tall curved stroke on the right.
items.selection_reason: It offers a distinct script-style comparison connected by its description to a vessel inscription, while paleographic accounts report varied forms and competing interpretations.

limitations.text: These are modern redrawings, not artifact photographs or direct facsimiles. The bronze-style redraw is associated with a vessel inscription, but the images do not establish a chronological path or decide among the proposed analyses involving 斤, 辛, 木, or 𣓀.
